Working Capital Management: Cycle, Inventory and Receivables

Working capital is the money tied up in running the business each day. Too little and bills go unpaid; too much and capital sits idle. This guide covers how it is measured and managed.

2 min readFor MBA, BBA and BBMUpdated 2 November 2026

Gross and net working capital

Gross working capital means total current assets. Net working capital means current assets minus current liabilities. Permanent working capital is the minimum always needed, while temporary working capital rises and falls with the season.

The operating cycle

Cash conversion cycle = inventory days + receivable days − payable days = 45 + 30 − 35 = 40 days.

Here, the firm funds 40 days of operations itself. A shorter cycle frees up cash. Large retailers often run a negative cycle, because they collect from customers before paying suppliers.

Managing inventory

  • EOQ finds the order size at which ordering and holding costs are lowest in total.
  • ABC analysis: control the few high-value items closely (A) and the many low-value items loosely (C).
  • Just-in-time keeps stock low, but relies on suppliers.
  • Reorder level = daily use × lead time + safety stock.

EOQ = √(2 × annual demand × cost per order ÷ holding cost per unit). With demand of 12,000 units, ₹500 per order and ₹30 holding cost: √(2 × 12,000 × 500 ÷ 30) = √4,00,000 = about 632 units.

Managing receivables and payables

  • Credit policy trades off higher sales against slower cash and bad debts.
  • Offer a discount for early payment, such as 2/10 net 30: 2% off if paid in 10 days, otherwise due in 30.
  • Track the ageing of receivables, so that late payers are noticed early.
  • Factoring and bill discounting turn receivables into cash, at a cost.
  • Stretching payables saves cash, but can hurt supplier relationships.

How working capital is financed

SourceNote
Trade creditSuppliers' credit, usually the cheapest
Cash credit and overdraftBank limits against stock and receivables
Bill discounting and factoringEarly cash against invoices
Commercial paperFor highly rated firms
Long-term fundsPrudent for the permanent part

Three financing approaches

A conservative approach uses long-term funds for most working capital, which is safe but costlier. An aggressive approach uses short-term funds even for the permanent part, which is cheaper but riskier. A matching (hedging) approach funds permanent needs with long-term money and temporary needs with short-term money.

Exam and interview questions

What is the difference between gross and net working capital?

Gross working capital is total current assets. Net working capital is current assets minus current liabilities.

Can working capital be negative?

Yes. It is normal for some retailers and subscription businesses, which collect cash quickly. For most other firms, it may signal liquidity trouble.

What is the operating cycle?

The time from buying raw materials to collecting cash from customers. Subtract the credit period from suppliers to get the cash conversion cycle.
